title.narrative: Strengthening Institutional capacities for equitable justice delivery and sustainable economic development.

description.narrative: The rule of law, effective access to justice and sustainable economic development are central to ensuring respect for human rights, fundamental freedoms, and enjoyment of equitable development. India’s rapid economic growth over the past decade has created new opportunities for prosperity, employment, and innovation. Yet, the benefits of this growth have not been evenly shared. Persistent socio-economic inequalities, environmental degradation, and justice deficits continue to challenge inclusive and sustainable development, particularly for marginalized groups including women, Scheduled Castes and Tribes, religious minorities, persons with disabilities, and informal workers. These inequities are compounded by limited access to justice and weak accountability frameworks that constrain the full realization of rights and entitlements.At the same time, India’s justice delivery system faces structural constraints including over 50 million pending cases, low judicial capacity, and inadequate access to affordable legal aid. Women and other vulnerable populations remain disproportionately excluded from formal justice processes due to financial, cultural, and procedural barriers, as well as limited gender representation within the justice system itself. Although digital innovations such as the e-Courts Mission Mode Project, Tele-Law, and the application of artificial intelligence in courts have begun transforming access, the benefits of such reforms remain uneven, with the digital divide driven by geography, gender, caste, and income limiting their reach.Parallel to these justice challenges, India’s private sector plays a defining role in the country’s economic transformation. However, fragmented regulatory frameworks, weak enforcement of responsible business standards, and limited awareness of human rights obligations among enterprises especially micro, small and medium enterprises undermine equitable growth.
